problem:
The unit square $D$ has vertices $(1,0),(0,0),(0,1),(1,1).$ What is the area of the image of $D$ under the action of the linear transformation $T$ with the standard matrix $T,$ given below?

$$
T=[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 \\ 1 & 1\end{aligned}]
$$

feedback.problem:
The triangle $D$ has vertices $(2,1),(6,1),(5,4).$ What is the area of the image of $D$ under the action of the linear transformation $T$ with the standard matrix $T,$ given below?

$$
T=[\begin{aligned}4 & 1 \\ -3 & 1\end{aligned}]
$$

$\text{Area}(T(D))=$
{{field-1}}
feedback.worked_solution:
First, let's sketch our region:

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14062337/assets/92ee29a22baa10f4af25db8221e7d67c729f5f0f1b5e1b3c37aee7e31a92bdfb.png)

Recall that for any linear transformation $T,$ we have the following connection between the area of $D$ and the area of the image $T(D)$ under the action of $T:$

$$
\text{Area}(T(D))=|det(T)|\cdot \text{Area}(D).
$$

From the diagram, we have

$$
\text{Area}(D)=\frac{1}{2}\cdot 4\cdot 3=6.
$$

Computing the determinant of $T,$ we get 

$$
det(T)=4\cdot 1-1\cdot (-3)=4+3=7.
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{Area}(T(D)) & =|det(T)|\cdot \text{Area}(D) \\  & =|\,7\,|\cdot 6 \\  & =42.\end{aligned}
$$
